items.samhita_patha: दि॒वस्पृ॑थि॒व्या अ॒न्तरि॑क्षात्समु॒द्राद॒ग्नेर्वाता॑न्मधुक॒शा हि ज॒ज्ञे। तां चा॑यि॒त्वामृतं॒ वसा॑नां हृ॒द्भिः प्र॒जाः प्रति॑ नन्दन्ति॒ सर्वाः॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Verily from sky, from earth, from atmosphere, from ocean, from fire, from wind was born the honey-whip; noting ( cāy ) it, [as] putting on immortality, all creatures ( prajā́ ) rejoice to meet it with their hearts.
commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊Partly prose—14 a and 21 to the end.⌋ Found also ⌊with vs. 3 before 2, vs. 7 before 6, and vs. 18 before 16⌋ in Pāipp. xvi.; ⌊but according to a note in W's Collation-book, vss. 1-24 occur in Pāipp. at folios 226 a, 108 a, 69 b, i.e. in several different kāṇḍas! ⌋. The hymn is called the madhusūkta 'honey-hymn' in Vāit. 16. 12, and is prescribed to be recited to accompany the mixing of soma with milk in a part of the agniṣṭoma ceremony. It is reckoned to the varcasya gaṇa (see note to Kāuç. 12. 10); and (always in company with iii. 16; vi. 69) is directed in Kāuç. 10. 24*; 12. 15; 13. 6 to be recited in various ceremonies. ⌊See also notes to vss. 13, 18.⌋ *⌊vi. 125. 2 and ix. 1. 1 and xix. 3. 1 have the same pratīka ( divaspṛthivyās ). SPP. understands the comm. at iii. 16 and at vi. 69 as intending ix. 1 by divaspṛthivyās ⌋ but the comm. at xix. 3 understands xix. 3 as intended (cf. Whitney's introduction to xix. 3).—The "honeyed whip," mádhumatī káçā , of the Açvins is mentioned in the RV. (i. 22. 3; 157. 4). Oldenberg, Rel. des Veda , p. 209, thinks it refers to the morning dew. Cf. Macdonell, Ved. Mythol. , p. 49, 54.⌋ The irregularities of meter in a and c may be rectified ⌊very unsatisfactorily⌋ by combining pṛthivyā́ ’nt- (as Ppp. actually reads) and resolving cāyitu-ā́ . Divás p- is prescribed by Prāt. ii. 68.

commentaries.whitney: Great, all-formed [is] the milk of it; also they call thee the seed of ocean; whence the granting honey-whip cometh, thither breath, thither immortality ( amṛ́ta ) hath entered in.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. puts payas in a after viçvarūpam ⌊and combines payo ‘syās⌋ and puts tvā in b after uta; and it reads at the end diviṣṭaṁ . It also gives the verse after our vs. 3. The metrical definition of the Anukr. is wrong, since a fair triṣṭubh is restorable by a little resolution ( viçu-a , pṛ-āṇas ).

items.samhita_patha: पश्य॑न्त्यस्याश्चरि॒तं पृ॑थि॒व्यां पृथ॒ङ्नरो॑ बहु॒धा मीमां॑समानाः। अ॒ग्नेर्वाता॑न्मधुक॒शा हि ज॒ज्ञे म॒रुता॑मु॒ग्रा न॒प्तिः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Men, manifoldly meditating ( mimāṅs- ) severally see its movement ( caritá ) on the earth; verily from fire, from wind was born the honey-whip, the formidable daughter ( naptí ) of the Maruts.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Pāda c is identical with 1 b , pādas c, d with 10 c, d . Ppp. reads at end of a pṛthivyāṣ; at end of d , ugrā anapatiḥ (also in vs. 10).

commentaries.whitney: Mother of the Ādityas, daughter of the Vasus, breath of creatures ( prajā́ ), navel of immortality ( amṛ́ta ), gold-colored, dripping with ghee ( ghṛtā́cī ), the honey-whip moves among mortals [as] a great brightness (bhárga).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Bp.p.m., Bp. 2 T. read gárbhas in d , and our edition follows them, doubtless erroneously. ⌊All of SPP's authorities give bhárgas .⌋ With a, b compare RV. viii. 101 (90). 15 a, b ⌊and MB. ii. 8. 15 a, b ⌋. The Anukr. does not heed the redundant syllable in c . ⌊Correct gárbhaç to bhárgaç .⌋

items.samhita_patha: मधोः॒ कशा॑मजनयन्त दे॒वास्तस्या॒ गर्भो॑ अभवद्वि॒श्वरू॑पः। तं जा॒तं तरु॑णं पिपर्ति मा॒ता स जा॒तो विश्वा॒ भुव॑ना॒ वि च॑ष्टे ॥

commentaries.whitney: The gods generated the whip of honey; of it there came to be an all-formed embryo; this, when born [and] tender, its mother fills; it, [when] born, looks abroad on all existences.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. has at the end bhuvanā ’bhi vaste .

items.samhita_patha_plain: मधोः कशामजनयन्त देवास्तस्या गर्भो अभवद्विश्वरूपः। तं जातं तरुणं पिपर्ति माता स जातो विश्वा भुवना वि चष्टे ॥

items.samhita_patha: कस्तं प्र वे॑द॒ क उ॒ तं चि॑केत॒ यो अ॑स्या हृ॒दः क॒लशः॑ सोम॒धानो॒ अक्षि॑तः। ब्र॒ह्मा सु॑मे॒धाः सो अ॑स्मिन्मदेत ॥

commentaries.whitney: Who knows ( pra-vid ) that, who understands ( cit ) that which [is] the unexhausted soma-holding vessel of the heart of it? The priest ( brahmán ) of excellent wisdom—he may revel in it.
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Of it' ( b ) is fem., and so relates to the 'honey-whip'; 'in it,' at the end, relates to the 'vessel.' Akṣitas (Ppp. akṣatas ) at the end of b is plainly an intrusive addition to the pāda; the Anukr., wrongly reckoning the initial a of asyās as unelided, counts 15 syllables in the pāda, and calls both this and the next verse by the unusual and indefinite name mahābṛhatī .

commentaries.whitney: He knows those two, he understands them that [are] its two unexhausted, thousand-streaming breasts; they milk out refreshment ( ū́rj ), unresisting.
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Its,' i.e. of the 'honey-whip.' Ppp. reads again akṣatāu in b , and it puts this verse before our vs. 6.

commentaries.whitney: She that, crying much, great, vigor-bestowing, loud-noised, goes unto her course (? vratá ), bellowing at three gharmás —she lows a lowing, she abounds ( pī ) with milk ( páyas ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Crying loudly,' lit. 'making to excess the sound hing '; 'abounds with milk,' perhaps rather 'gives milk in streams.' The verse is very obscure; it is in part identical with 10. 6 below (= RV. i. 164. 28). Its irregular meter (11 + 10 [11?]: 9 + 11 = 41 syllables) is very ill defined by the Anukr. ⌊which seems to scan as 11 + 9: 9 + 11⌋.

items.samhita_patha_plain: हिङ्करिक्रती बृहती वयोधा उच्चैर्घोषाभ्येति या व्रतम्। त्रीन्घर्मानभि वावशाना मिमाति मायुं पयते पयोभिः ॥

commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Whom' is fem.; 'they' ( c ) is masc, = the bulls. Parts of this verse and the following one are lost in Ppp. The Anukr. ⌊seems to scan as 11 + 11: 9 + 9⌋.

items.samhita_patha: स्त॑नयि॒त्नुस्ते॒ वाक्प्र॑जापते॒ वृषा॒ शुष्मं॑ क्षिपसि॒ भूम्या॒मधि॑। अ॒ग्नेर्वाता॑न्मधुक॒शा हि ज॒ज्ञे म॒रुता॑मु॒ग्रा न॒प्तिः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Thunder [is] thy voice, O Prajāpati; a bull, thou castest ( kṣip ) vehemence (? çúṣma ) over the earth; verily from fire, from wind was born the honey-whip, the formidable daughter of the Maruts.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The latter half-verse we had above, as 3 c, d ; the former half-verse is repeated below, as 20 a, b ⌊with diví for ádhi at the end⌋. ⌊Bloomfield thinks çuṣma is 'lightning': ZDMG. xlviii. 566.⌋ O. reads at the beginning stanayitnúṣ ṭe . The metrical description of the Anukr. means only that the syllables are 40 in all (10 + 12: 11 + 7), and that one pāda contains seven.

items.samhita_patha: यथा॒ सोमः॑ प्रातःसव॒ने अ॒श्विनो॑र्भवति प्रि॒यः। ए॒वा मे॑ अश्विना॒ वर्च॑ आ॒त्मनि॑ ध्रियताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: As at the early pressing soma is loved ( priyá ) of the Açvins, so, O Açvins, let splendor be maintained in my self.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यथा सोमः प्रातःसवने अश्विनोर्भवति प्रियः। एवा मे अश्विना वर्च आत्मनि ध्रियताम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: यथा॒ सोमो॑ द्वि॒तीये॒ सव॑न इन्द्रा॒ग्न्योर्भ॑वति प्रि॒यः। ए॒वा म॑ इन्द्राग्नी॒ वर्च॑ आ॒त्मनि॑ ध्रियताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: As at the second pressing soma is loved of Indra-and-Agni, so, O Indra-and-Agni, let splendor be maintained in my self.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यथा सोमो द्वितीये सवन इन्द्राग्न्योर्भवति प्रियः। एवा म इन्द्राग्नी वर्च आत्मनि ध्रियताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: As at the third pressing soma is loved of the Ṛibhus, so, O Ṛibhus, let splendor be maintained in my self.

items.samhita_patha: मधु॑ जनिषीय॒ मधु॑ वंशिषीय। पय॑स्वानग्न॒ आग॑मं॒ तं मा॒ सं सृ॑ज॒ वर्च॑सा ॥

commentaries.whitney: May I generate honey; may I win honey; rich in milk, O Agni, have I come; unite me here with splendor.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The second part of the verse we have had above as vii. 89. 1 c, d . The edition reads, with all the mss., vaṅçiṣīya , but it should be emended to vaṅsiṣīya (root van ); cf. the similar misreading at xvi. 9. 4. Ppp. reads madhu janiṣī manu mambikīyah; and it combines agnā "gamaṁ . By reckoning the first part of the passage as metrical (which it is not) the Anukr. counts out a good purauṣṇih .

items.samhita_patha_plain: मधु जनिषीय मधु वंशिषीय। पयस्वानग्न आगमं तं मा सं सृज वर्चसा ॥

items.samhita_patha: सं मा॑ग्ने॒ वर्च॑सा सृज॒ सं प्र॒जया॒ समायु॑षा। वि॒द्युर्मे॑ अ॒स्य दे॒वा इन्द्रो॑ विद्यात्स॒ह ऋषि॑भिः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Unite me, O Agni, with splendor, with progeny, with life-time; may the gods know me as such; may Indra know, together with the seers.
commentaries.whitney_notes: We had the verse above, as vii. 89. 2.

items.samhita_patha_plain: सं माग्ने वर्चसा सृज सं प्रजया समायुषा। विद्युर्मे अस्य देवा इन्द्रो विद्यात्सह ऋषिभिः ॥

items.samhita_patha: यथा॒ मधु॑ मधु॒कृतः॑ सं॒भर॑न्ति॒ मधा॒वधि॑। ए॒वा मे॑ अश्विना॒ वर्च॑ आ॒त्मनि॑ ध्रियताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: As the honey-makers bring together honey upon honey, so, O Açvins, let splendor be maintained in my self.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads, for the second half-verse, evā me 'çvinā balam ojaç ca dhriyatām: cf. our 17 c, d . The line is, like the corresponding parts of 11-13, not metrical as it stands.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यथा मधु मधुकृतः संभरन्ति मधावधि। एवा मे अश्विना वर्च आत्मनि ध्रियताम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: यथा॒ मक्षा॑ इ॒दं मधु॑ न्य॒ञ्जन्ति॒ मधा॒वधि॑। ए॒वा मे॑ अश्विना॒ वर्च॒स्तेजो॒ बल॒मोज॑श्च ध्रियताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: As the flies ( mákṣā ) smear down here honey upon honey, so, O Açvins, let my splendor, brilliancy, strength, and force be maintained.
commentaries.whitney_notes: In a , delete the superfluous accent-mark under dhu . Ppp. has quite another version of a, b : yathā makṣā mayuntyujaṁ dakṣiṇām adhi: and it omits balam ojas in d . The omission of any one of the three nouns in our d would rectify the meter.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यथा मक्षा इदं मधु न्यञ्जन्ति मधावधि। एवा मे अश्विना वर्चस्तेजो बलमोजश्च ध्रियताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: What honey on hills ( girí ), on mountains, what in kine, in horses, in strong drink ( súrā ) as poured out, what honey [is] there, [be] that in me.
commentaries.whitney_notes: With this verse and the next are to be compared vi. 69. 1, 2 ⌊where the use by Vāit. is given⌋. Ppp. has only yadi giriṣyavipāṁ citviṣī in place of this verse, and puts it before our 16.

commentaries.whitney: O ye Açvins, lords of beauty! anoint me with the honey of bees ( sāraghá ), that I may speak splendid words among the people.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This verse differs only by one word from vi. 69. 2.

items.samhita_patha: स्त॑नयि॒त्नुस्ते॒ वाक्प्र॑जापते॒ वृषा॒ शुष्मं॑ क्षिपसि॒ भूम्यां॑ दि॒वि। तां प॒शव॒ उप॑ जीवन्ति॒ सर्वे॒ तेनो॒ सेष॒मूर्जं॑ पिपर्ति ॥

commentaries.whitney: Thunder [is] thy voice, O Prajāpati; a bull, thou castest vehemence on the earth, on the sky; upon that live all cattle; with this it lavishes ( pṛ ) food ( íṣ ) [and] refreshment.

items.samhita_patha_plain: स्तनयित्नुस्ते वाक्प्रजापते वृषा शुष्मं क्षिपसि भूम्यां दिवि। तां पशव उप जीवन्ति सर्वे तेनो सेषमूर्जं पिपर्ति ॥

items.samhita_patha: पृ॑थि॒वी द॒ण्डो॒न्तरि॑क्षं॒ गर्भो॒ द्यौः कशा॑ वि॒द्युत्प्र॑क॒शो हि॑र॒ण्ययो॑ बि॒न्दुः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Earth [is] the staff, atmosphere the embryo, sky the whip, lightning the snapper (? prakaçá ), of gold the globule ( bindú ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The Pet. Lex. conjectures "Peitschenriemen" for prakaçá . Ppp. leaves the initial of antarikṣam unelided, and for prakaças has prakāçā madhokaçā ci ghṛtācī .

items.samhita_patha_plain: पृथिवी दण्डोन्तरिक्षं गर्भो द्यौः कशा विद्युत्प्रकशो हिरण्ययो बिन्दुः ॥

items.samhita_patha: यो वै कशा॑याः स॒प्त मधू॑नि॒ वेद॒ मधु॑मान्भवति। ब्रा॑ह्म॒णश्च॒ राजा॑ च धे॒नुश्चा॑न॒ड्वांश्च॑ व्री॒हिश्च॒ यव॑श्च॒ मधु॑ सप्त॒मम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: He who knows the seven honeys of the whip becomes rich in honey: the Brahman, and the king, and the milch-cow, and the draft-ox, and rice, and barley; honey the seventh.
commentaries.whitney_notes: One does not see why the Anukr. calls the passage brāhmī purauṣṇih ⌊that is 6 ⁄ 4 of 12: 8 + 8 = 18: 12 + 12 = 42⌋ rather than simply brāhmī uṣṇih ⌊ 6 ⁄ 4 of 8 + 8: 12 = 12 + 12: 18 = 42⌋; it is the only example of either name in the treatise. ⌊The not very sufficient reason for the preference would seem to be the position of the avasāna , which divides the "vs." as 18:24 and not as 24: 18.⌋ ⌊Ppp. has in a madhukaçāyās for kaç- and sapta madhumatīm for madhumān bhavati; then follows madhumato lokāṅ jayati (cf. vs. 23).⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: यो वै कशायाः सप्त मधूनि वेद मधुमान्भवति। ब्राह्मणश्च राजा च धेनुश्चानड्वांश्च व्रीहिश्च यवश्च मधु सप्तमम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Rich in honey he becomes; rich in honey becomes his provision ( āhāryà ); worlds rich in honey he conquers, who knows thus.

commentaries.whitney: When it thunders in a clear sky, that is Prajāpati himself becoming manifest to his creatures; therefore I stand with the sacred cord over the right shoulder, saying: O Prajāpati, take notice ( anu-budh ) of me: creatures [take notice], Prajāpati takes notice of him who knows thus.
commentaries.whitney_notes: In order to make an aṣṭi (64 syll.) of this piece of prose, we have to restore ánu and separate íti in d , and to resolve ánu enam in e ; and to make six pādas the last line has to be violently divided; the pada -text intimates a division after the second ánu . ⌊Ppp. in a-b has a tat also before prajāpatis and in e it reads prajā budhyante for prajāp- budhyate .⌋ ⌊The hymn begins with divás and the quoted Anukr. says "divaç" ca catur-uttarāḥ (referring to a plus of 4 over the normal 20).⌋

commentaries.whitney: Of the props ( upamít ), of the supports ( pratimít ), and also of the connectors (? parimít ) of the dwelling ( çā́lā ) that possesses all choice things, we unfasten the tied ( naddhá ) [parts].
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads upamitaṣ pratimito ‘tho parimitaç ca yaç çālāyā viçvavārāyā te naddhān vi cṛtāmasi .

items.samhita_patha_plain: उपमितां प्रतिमितामथो परिमितामुत। शालाया विश्ववाराया नद्धानि वि चृतामसि ॥

items.samhita_patha: यत्ते॑ न॒द्धं वि॑श्ववारे॒ पाशो॑ ग्र॒न्थिश्च॒ यः कृ॒तः। बृह॒स्पति॑रिवा॒हं ब॒लं वा॒चा वि स्रं॑सयामि॒ तत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: What of thee is tied, O thou that possessest all choice things, what fetter and knot is made, that with a spell ( vā́c ) I make fall apart, as Brihaspati [did] Bala.
commentaries.whitney_notes: All the mss. read balám (not valám ) in c , as also Ppp. ( bṛhaspatiṁ vahaṁ balam ). Our Bp. has in d sraṅçayāmi: tvát . The Anukr. seems to imply the abbreviation of iva to ’va in c .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यत्ते नद्धं विश्ववारे पाशो ग्रन्थिश्च यः कृतः। बृहस्पतिरिवाहं बलं वाचा वि स्रंसयामि तत् ॥

items.samhita_patha: आ य॑याम॒ सं ब॑बर्ह ग्र॒न्थींश्च॑कार ते दृ॒ढान्। परूं॑षि वि॒द्वाञ्छस्ते॒वेन्द्रे॑ण॒ वि चृ॑तामसि ॥

commentaries.whitney: He stretched ( ā-yam ), he combined ( sam-bṛh ), he made thy knots firm ( dṛḍhá ); with Indra we unfasten [them], as a knowing slaughterer the joints.
commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊Partly prose—25 to end.⌋ Found also in Pāipp. xvi. (in the verse-order 1-3, 5, 4, 6-10, 14, 16, 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 21, 18, 20, 19, 24, 23, 22, 25-31). The hymn is not noticed in Vāit.; but several verses (1, 15, 18, 22, 24) are quoted in Kāuç. 66. 22-30, in connection with an inauguration-ceremony ( savayajña ) in which a house (a toy house?) is an object given. Translated: Ludwig, p. 464; Zimmer, p. 151 (vss. 1-24); Grill, 60, 188 (vss. 1-24); Henry, 87, 121; Griffith, i. 434; Bloomfield, 193, 595.—Cf. also Oldenberg, IFA. vi. 179.

items.samhita_patha: वं॒शानां॑ ते॒ नह॑नानां प्राणा॒हस्य॒ तृण॑स्य च। प॒क्षाणां॑ विश्ववारे ते न॒द्धानि॒ वि चृ॑तामसि ॥

commentaries.whitney: Of thy beams ( vaṅçá ), ties ( náhana ), and binding ( prāṇāhá ) grass, of thy sides ( pakṣá ), O thou that possessest all choice things, we unfasten the tied [parts].
commentaries.whitney_notes: Vaṅçá is properly a bamboo beam. Prāṇāhá (unchanged in pada -text) seems to occur only here, nor is root nah elsewhere combined with pra; I have ventured to render it as an adj., as tṛ́ṇa appears to call for a descriptive epithet. Ppp. reads naddhān vi in d .

items.samhita_patha_plain: वंशानां ते नहनानां प्राणाहस्य तृणस्य च। पक्षाणां विश्ववारे ते नद्धानि वि चृतामसि ॥

items.samhita_patha: सं॑दं॒शानां॑ पल॒दानां॒ परि॑ष्वञ्जल्यस्य च। इ॒दं मान॑स्य॒ पत्न्या॑ न॒द्धानि॒ वि चृ॑तामसि ॥
items.pada_patha: स॒म्ऽदं॒शाना॑म् । प॒ल॒दाना॑म् । परि॑ऽस्वञ्जल्यस्य । च॒ । इ॒दम् । मान॑स्य । पत्न्या॑: । न॒ध्दानि॑ । वि । चृ॒ता॒म॒सि॒ ॥३.५॥

commentaries.whitney:
Of the clamps ( saṁdaṅçá ), of the paladás , and of the embracer
( páriṣvañjalya )—now of the mistress of the building do we unfasten the tied [parts].
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads, in a, b , palidānāṁ pariṣvañcanadasya ca; and, for c , sarvā mānasya patni te; it also puts the verse before our 4.

items.samhita_patha_plain: संदंशानां पलदानां परिष्वञ्जल्यस्य च। इदं मानस्य पत्न्या नद्धानि वि चृतामसि ॥

items.samhita_patha: यानि॑ ते॒ऽन्तः शि॒क्या᳡न्याबे॒धू र॒ण्या॑य॒ कम्। प्र ते॒ तानि॑ चृतामसि शि॒वा मा॑नस्य पत्नी न॒ उद्धि॑ता त॒न्वे᳡ भव ॥

commentaries.whitney: What hanging vessels (? çikyà ) they bound on to thee within for enjoyment, those we unfasten for thee; be thou, [when] set up, O mistress of the building, propitious to our self ( tanū́ ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Çikyà may be an ornamental hanging appendage of some kind.* All the mss. read mā́nasya patni in d ; our edition emends to mān- . The pada -text has úddhitā , undivided, in e (as at xviii. 2. 34, and uddhíḥ at viii. 8. 22); the case ought to fall under Prāt. iv. 62, but root dhā is not mentioned there, though we find han superfluously included. Ppp. reads yāni te antaç cikyāny āmedho ‘ntyāya kaṁ; and, for d , sarvā mānasya patnyā. *⌊As to decorations of this kind, see John Griffiths, The Paintings in the Buddhist Cave-Temples of Ajantâ , London, 1896, plates 6, 10, and 13; of. also Karpūra-mañjarī, iii. 27, ed. Konow, and my note thereon at p. 289. W. has interlined "slings" as an alternative rendering of çikyà .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: यानि तेऽन्तः शिक्या᳡न्याबेधू रण्याय कम्। प्र ते तानि चृतामसि शिवा मानस्य पत्नी न उद्धिता तन्वे᳡ भव ॥

commentaries.whitney: Oblation-holder ( havirdhā́na ), fire-place ( agniçā́la ), wives' site [and] seat; seat of the gods art thou, O heavenly dwelling.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The paroṣṇih is regular, save for the common variant of a triṣṭubh instead of a jagatī -pāda at the end.

items.samhita_patha_plain: हविर्धानमग्निशालं पत्नीनां सदनं सदः। सदो देवानामसि देवि शाले ॥

items.samhita_patha: अक्षु॒मोप॒शं वित॑तं सहस्रा॒क्षं वि॑षू॒वति॑। अव॑नद्धम॒भिहि॑तं॒ ब्रह्म॑णा॒ वि चृ॑तामसि ॥

commentaries.whitney: The thousand-eyed net ( ákṣu ), stretched out as opaçá on the division-line ( viṣūvánt ), tied down, put on, do we with worship ( bráhman ) unfasten.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Abhihita in c doubtless contains the suggestion of abhidhāni 'a halter.' Geldner ( Ved. Stud. i. 136) wants to make of akṣu a 'stake' or 'pillar.' Viṣūvant probably means the 'parting of the hair, crown' (so Zimmer), here the ridge of the roof. Ppp. begins with yakṣmopiçam , and has in c the easier reading apinaddham apihitam .

items.samhita_patha_plain: अक्षुमोपशं विततं सहस्राक्षं विषूवति। अवनद्धमभिहितं ब्रह्मणा वि चृतामसि ॥

items.samhita_patha: यस्त्वा॑ शाले प्रतिगृ॒ह्णाति॒ येन॒ चासि॑ मि॒ता त्वम्। उ॒भौ मा॑नस्य पत्नि॒ तौ जीव॑तां ज॒रद॑ष्टी ॥

commentaries.whitney: He who, O dwelling, accepts thee, and he by whom thou art built—let both those, O mistress of the building, live to attain old age.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The mā́nasya of the mss. in c is again emended in our edition to mān- . Ppp. rectifies the meter of a by reading yaç citrā (ca tvā?) pr- . The Anukr. pays no heed to the irregularity of the verse (9 + 8: 8 + 7).

items.samhita_patha_plain: यस्त्वा शाले प्रतिगृह्णाति येन चासि मिता त्वम्। उभौ मानस्य पत्नि तौ जीवतां जरदष्टी ॥

items.samhita_patha: अ॒मुत्रै॑न॒मा ग॑च्छताद्दृ॒ढा न॒द्धा परि॑ष्कृता। यस्या॑स्ते विचृ॒ताम॒स्यङ्ग॑मङ्गं॒ परु॑ष्परुः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Do thou, made firm, tied, adorned ( pari-kṛ ), go to him yonder—thou whose every limb, whose every joint we unfasten.
commentaries.whitney_notes: O. reads in a amútrāi ’ṇam . Páriṣkṛtā is unaltered in the pada -text, as prescribed by Prāt. iv. 58. Enam probably indicates the "acceptor" (9 a , 15). Ppp. reads in b tridhā for dṛḍhā , and begins c with tasyas . ⌊As to amútra , cf. Oldenberg, IFA. vi. 179.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: अमुत्रैनमा गच्छताद्दृढा नद्धा परिष्कृता। यस्यास्ते विचृतामस्यङ्गमङ्गं परुष्परुः ॥

commentaries.whitney: He who fixed ( ni-mi ) thee, O dwelling, [who] brought together the forest trees—unto progeny, O dwelling, he, [as a] most exalted Prajāpati, made thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads pūrvas for çāle in a .

commentaries.whitney: Homage to him, homage to the giver, and to the lord of the dwelling we pay; homage to the forth-moving ( pra-car ) fire, and to thy spirit (? púruṣa ) [be] homage.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in b kṛṇmasi .

commentaries.whitney: Homage to kine, to horses, whatever is born ( vi-jā ) in the dwelling; thou rich in births ( vijā- ), rich in progeny, we unfasten thy fetters.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. lacks, probably by an oversight, the second half-verse.

commentaries.whitney: Thou coverest within the fire, the men together with the cattle ( paçú ); thou rich in births, rich in progeny, we unfasten thy fetters.

commentaries.whitney: Between both heaven and earth what expanse [there is], therewith do I accept this dwelling of thine; the atmosphere that pervades ( vimā́na ) space ( rájas ), that do I make a paunch ( udára ) for treasures; therewith I accept the house for this man.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This verse in Kāuç. 66. 28 accompanies the "acceptance" of the house in question. The Anukr. calls it an atiçakvarī , though it contains only 57 syllables (12 + 12: 11 + 11: 11) instead of 60. Ppp. reads at end of b tāi ’māṁ (an abbreviation which is here acceptable, as making a good triṣṭubh —pāda ⌊such was the case at ix. 2. 7 also⌋), and in e yac chālāṁ for tena ç- .

commentaries.whitney: Rich in refreshment, rich in milk, fixed ( ni-mi ), built upon the earth, bearing all food, O dwelling, do not thou injure those accepting [thee].

commentaries.whitney: Wrapped ( ā-vṛ ) with grass, clothing itself in paladás , the dwelling, place of rest ( nivéçanī ) of living creatures, like the night—built on the earth thou standest, like a she-elephant, having feet.
commentaries.whitney_notes: That is, apparently, heavy and big on the four corner posts, like an elephant (female because 'dwelling' is feminine) on its feet. With b compare xii. i. 6 b . The verse as a prastārapan̄kti (11 + 12: 8 + 8) has no irregularity which the Anukr. is wont to heed.

commentaries.whitney: Of thy rush-work ( íṭa ) I unfasten what was tied on, uncovering; [thee] pressed together by Varuṇa let Mitra in the morning open out.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The verse in Kāuç. 66. 24 accompanies the letting down ( ava-sṛ ) of the door. ⌊Bergaigne has a note on the vs., Rel. Véd. iii. 122.⌋

commentaries.whitney: The dwelling fixed with worship ( bráhman ), fixed, built by the poets—let Indra-and-Agni, immortal, defend the dwelling, the seat for soma ( somyá ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: P. reads nírmitām in b , and sāumyám in d . Ppp. has a quite different version: catussraktiṁ paricakrāṁ for a ; viçvāna bibhratī çālām (cf. our 16 c ) amṛto sāumyaṁ sadaḥ for c, d .

commentaries.whitney:
A nest ( kulā́ya ) upon a nest, a vessel ( kóça ) pressed together in a vessel—there a mortal is born ( vi-jā ), from whom all is generated
( pra-jā ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. has martyas in c .

commentaries.whitney: [The dwelling] which is fixed with two sides, with four sides, which with six sides—the eight-sided, the ten-sided dwelling, the mistress of the building, Agni lies in like an embryo.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -text reads aṣṭā॰pakṣām in c , by Prāt. iii. 2; iv. 94. ⌊As to pakṣa , cf. iii. 7. 3.⌋ The verse is a good pan̄kti , involving only the resolution mā́nasi-a in d , but the Anukr. absurdly treats it as of four pādas; and, in accordance with this, the pada -mss. mark a pāda division after çā́lām .

items.samhita_patha: प्र॒तीचीं॑ त्वा प्रती॒चीनः॒ शाले॒ प्रैम्यहिं॑सतीम्। अ॒ग्निर्ह्य१॒॑न्तराप॑श्च॒र्तस्य॑ प्रथ॒मा द्वाः ॥

commentaries.whitney: I go forward, O dwelling, turned toward thee, uninjuring, that art turned toward me; for within [are] fire and waters, the first door of right ( ṛtá ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads at the end prathamobhā . The mss. all have ca rtásya in c-d . The verse is quoted in Kāuç. 66. 25, accompanying the action of 'going forward with ( ādāya ) water-pot [and] fire.'

items.samhita_patha_plain: प्रतीचीं त्वा प्रतीचीनः शाले प्रैम्यहिंसतीम्। अग्निर्ह्य१न्तरापश्चर्तस्य प्रथमा द्वाः ॥

items.samhita_patha: इ॒मा आपः॒ प्र भ॑राम्यय॒क्ष्मा य॑क्ष्म॒नाश॑नीः। गृ॒हानुप॒ प्र सी॑दाम्य॒मृते॑न स॒हाग्निना॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: I bring forward these waters, free from yákṣma , dispellers of yákṣma ; I set forth unto the houses, together with immortal fire.
commentaries.whitney_notes: We had this verse above, as iii. 12. 9. Ppp. (which omitted it as part of that hymn) reads in a harāmi , and in c abhi (for upa ).

items.samhita_patha_plain: इमा आपः प्र भराम्ययक्ष्मा यक्ष्मनाशनीः। गृहानुप प्र सीदाम्यमृतेन सहाग्निना ॥

items.samhita_patha: मा नः॒ पाशं॒ प्रति॑ मुचो गु॒रुर्भा॒रो ल॒घुर्भ॑व। व॒धूमि॑व त्वा शाले यत्र॒कामं॑ भरामसि ॥

commentaries.whitney: Fasten thou not on us the fetter; a heavy burden, become thou light; like a woman ( vadhū́ ), O dwelling, we carry thee where we will.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Quoted in Kāuç. 66. 30. ⌊Cf. again Oldenberg, IFA. vi. 179.—Over "woman" W. interlines "bride?"⌋

commentaries.whitney: The bright bull of a thousand, rich in milk, bearing all forms in his bellies, desiring to accomplish (? çikṣ ) what is excellent for his giver, the sacrificer—he, the ruddy one of Brihaspati, hath stretched ⌊ ā-tan ⌋ the line ( tántu ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: That is, doubtless, 'has extended or performed the sacrifice.'

items.samhita_patha: अ॒पां यो अग्ने॑ प्रति॒मा ब॒भूव॑ प्र॒भूः सर्व॑स्मै पृथि॒वीव॑ दे॒वी। पि॒ता व॒त्सानां॒ पति॑र॒घ्न्यानां॑ साह॒स्रे पोषे॒ अपि॑ नः कृणोतु ॥

commentaries.whitney: He who in the beginning became the counterpart (pratimā́) of the waters, prevailing ( prabhū́ ) for everything, like the divine earth, father of young ( vatsá ), lord of the inviolable [kine]—let him set ( kṛ ) us in thousandfold prosperity.

items.samhita_patha_plain: अपां यो अग्ने प्रतिमा बभूव प्रभूः सर्वस्मै पृथिवीव देवी। पिता वत्सानां पतिरघ्न्यानां साहस्रे पोषे अपि नः कृणोतु ॥

commentaries.whitney: A male ( púmāṅs ), [yet] pregnant, big ( sthávira ), rich in milk, the bull bears a trunk ( kábandha ) of good ( vásu ); him, sacrificed to Indra, let Agni Jātavedas carry by the roads traveled by the gods.
commentaries.whitney_notes: W. reads in b vásoṣ ká- .

items.samhita_patha: पि॒ता व॒त्सानां॒ पति॑र॒घ्न्याना॒मथो॑ पि॒ता म॑ह॒तां गर्ग॑राणाम्। व॒त्सो ज॒रायु॑ प्रति॒धुक्पी॒यूष॑ आ॒मिक्षा॑ घृ॒तं तद्व॑स्य॒ रेतः॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Father of calves, lord of the inviolable [kine], also father of great gulfs ( gárgara ); calf, afterbirth, fresh milk, beestings, curd, ghee—that [is] his seed.
commentaries.whitney_notes: [ Brahman.—caturviṅçakam. ārṣabham. trāiṣṭubham: 8. bhurij; 6, 10, 24. jagatī; 11-17, 19, 20, 23. anuṣṭubh; 18. upariṣṭād bṛhatī; 21. āstārapan̄kti. ] Found also in Pāipp. xvi. (in the verse-order 1-3, 5, 4, 6, 8, 7, 9, 10-13, 15, 14, 16-22, 24, 23). Not noticed in Vāit., and not in Kāuç. in a way to cast any light whatever upon it; the hymn is quoted in Kāuç. 24. 19 (with vi. 111) in the ceremony of turning a bull loose, and vs. 24 separately in the same ceremony in Kāuç. 24. 21; also vs. 1 in 66. 18 in connection with a bull; the hymn is reckoned (see note to Kāuç. 19. 1) among the puṣṭika mantras . Translated: Henry, 90, 128; Griffith, i. 438.—For some of the vss. the reader may consult Hillebrandt, Ved. Myth. i. 330, 516, 382, 358, 525. The verse occurs also in TS. (iii. 3. 9 2 ), MS. (ii. 5. 10), and K. (xiii. 9). In b , MS. reads utā́ ’yám for átho; for d , TS. has āmíkṣā mástu ghṛtám asya rétaḥ , and MS. the same, save yóniḥ for rétaḥ .

commentaries.whitney: The gods' portion [was] that load, the sap of waters, of plants, of ghee; the mighty one ( çakrá ) chose a drink of soma; a great stone became what [was his] body.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This verse also is found in TS. and MS. (as above), in both texts preceding our vs. 4 (in MS. one other verse intervenes, our xviii. 4. 28). Both have, for a , devā́nām eṣá upanāhá āsīt; for b , TS. has apā́ṁ gárbha óṣahīṣu nyàktaḥ , and MS. apā́m pátir vṛṣabhá óṣadhīnām; in c , both have drapsám for bhakṣám and pūṣā́ for çakráḥ; in d , after abhavat , MS. has yát tád ā́sīt , and TS. tád eṣām .

items.samhita_patha_plain: देवानां भाग उपनाह एषोपां रस ओषधीनां घृतस्य। सोमस्य भक्षमवृणीत शक्रो बृहन्नद्रिरभवद्यच्छरीरम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: सोमे॑न पू॒र्णं क॒लशं॑ बिभर्षि॒ त्वष्टा॑ रू॒पाणां॑ जनि॒ता प॑शू॒नाम्। शि॒वास्ते॑ सन्तु प्रज॒न्व᳡ इ॒ह या इ॒मा न्य१॒॑स्मभ्यं॑ स्वधिते यच्छ॒ या अ॒मूः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Thou bearest a vessel filled with soma, shaper ( tvástṛ ) of forms, generator of cattle; propitious to thee be these pudenda (? prajanū́ ) that are here; to us, O ax, confirm those that are yonder.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads at the beginning somasya; its second half-verse is unintelligible. The verse is with no propriety called a jagatī (11 + 11: 13 + 12 = 47).

items.samhita_patha_plain: सोमेन पूर्णं कलशं बिभर्षि त्वष्टा रूपाणां जनिता पशूनाम्। शिवास्ते सन्तु प्रजन्व᳡ इह या इमा न्य१स्मभ्यं स्वधिते यच्छ या अमूः ॥

items.samhita_patha: आज्यं॑ बिभर्ति घृ॒तम॑स्य॒ रेतः॑ साह॒स्रः पोष॒स्तमु॑ य॒ज्ञमा॑हुः। इन्द्र॑स्य रू॒पमृ॑ष॒भो वसा॑नः॒ सो अ॒स्मान्दे॑वाः शि॒व ऐतु॑ द॒त्तः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Sacrificial butter he bears; ghee [is] his seed; thousandfold prosperity—that they call the sacrifice; the bull, clothing himself in Indra's form—let him, O gods, come propitious to us, being given.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in b sahasrapoṣas , and in d ‘smā and çivāi ’tu .

items.samhita_patha_plain: आज्यं बिभर्ति घृतमस्य रेतः साहस्रः पोषस्तमु यज्ञमाहुः। इन्द्रस्य रूपमृषभो वसानः सो अस्मान्देवाः शिव ऐतु दत्तः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Indra's force, Varuṇa's two arms, the Açvins' two shoulders, of the Maruts this hump; they who are wise, poets, who are skilful ( manīṣín ), call him Brihaspati brought together.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The verse has two jagatī -pādas, though called by the Anukr. simply bhurij . Read at the end of b kakút .

commentaries.whitney: Rich in milk, thou stretchest unto the people ( víç ) of the gods; thee they call Indra, thee Sarasvant; he gives a thousand [kine] with one face who makes offering ( ā-hu ) of a bull to a Brahman.
commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊Cf. Oldenberg, IFA. vi. 183.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: दैवीर्विशः पयस्वाना तनोषि त्वामिन्द्रं त्वां सरस्वन्तमाहुः। सहस्रं स एकमुखा ददाति यो ब्राह्मण ऋषभमाजुहोति ॥

items.samhita_patha: बृह॒स्पतिः॑ सवि॒ता ते॒ वयो॑ दधौ॒ त्वष्टु॑र्वा॒योः पर्या॒त्मा त॒ आभृ॑तः। अ॒न्तरि॑क्षे॒ मन॑सा त्वा जुहोमि ब॒र्हिष्टे॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी उ॒भे स्ता॑म् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Brihaspati, Savitar bestowed on thee vigor ( váyas ); from Tvashṭar, from Vāyu was brought forth thy soul ( ātmán ); with mind in the atmosphere I make offering ( hu ) of thee; let heaven-and-earth both be thy barhís .
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads manas for vayas in a . The Anukr. calls the verse jagatī , though two of its pādas are triṣṭubh .

items.samhita_patha_plain: बृहस्पतिः सविता ते वयो दधौ त्वष्टुर्वायोः पर्यात्मा त आभृतः। अन्तरिक्षे मनसा त्वा जुहोमि बर्हिष्टे द्यावापृथिवी उभे स्ताम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: He who goes speaking out greatly among the kine, like Indra among the gods—of that bull let the worshiper ( brahmán ) praise together the members excellently.
commentaries.whitney_notes: All our mss. (save O.) read, like the edition, tásya ṛṣa- in c , although the passage is quoted as example under the Prāt. rule (iii. 46) that a or ā + ṛ make ar . Ppp. reads in a āindrī ’va . The paddhati (note to Kāuç. 24. 19) has the verse whispered in the right ear of the released bull.

commentaries.whitney: His sides were Anumati's; his flanks (? anūvṛ́j ) were Bhaga's; of his knees ( aṣṭhīvánt ) Mitra said: those are wholly mine.
commentaries.whitney_notes: All the nouns are duals. The Anukr. takes no notice of the redundant syllable in c . ⌊Henry would emend thus: - vántābrav -, i.e. - vántā abrav -. Ppp. reads at the beginning pārçvay āstām .

commentaries.whitney: His rump was the Ādityas'; his two thighs were Brihaspati's; his tail [was] the heavenly wind's; therewith he shakes the herbs.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in b çroṇīy āstām .

commentaries.whitney: His breast ( kroḍá ) was Jāmiçaṅsa's; his vessel [was] maintained as Soma's, when all the gods, coming together, distributed ( vi-kalpay- ) the bull.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -text reads, like the saṁhitā , utthātúḥ , by Prāt. iv. 62. Ppp. combines gudā ”saṁ; it also makes our 14 c, d and 15 c, d exchange places. ⌊Ppp. puts yat before ṛṣabham , and for akalpayan it has vika ...(gap).⌋ We had jāmiçaṅsa above (ii. 10. 1) as 'imprecation of sisters'; the word does not occur elsewhere. What part of the bull is his 'vessel' is obscure. The first pāda has a redundant syllable.

items.samhita_patha_plain: क्रोड आसीज्जामिशंसस्य सोमस्य कलशो धृतः। देवाः संगत्य यत्सर्व ऋषभं व्यकल्पयन् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: क्रोड: । आसीत् । जामिऽशंसस्य । सोमस्य । कलश: । धृत: । देवा: । सम्ऽगत्य । यत् । सर्वे । ऋषभम् । विऽअकल्पयन् ॥४.१५॥

items.samhita_patha: ते कुष्ठि॑काः स॒रमा॑यै कु॒र्मेभ्यो॑ अदधुः श॒फान्। ऊब॑ध्यमस्य की॒टेभ्यः॑ श्वव॒र्तेभ्यो॑ अधारयन् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Those dew-claws ( kúṣṭhikā ) [were] Saramā's; they assigned the hoofs to the tortoises ( kūrmá ); the content of his bowels they maintained for the worms, the çavartás .
commentaries.whitney_notes: The mss. are divided between çavarta (P.s.m.I.O.R.p.m.T.D.Kp.) and çvavarta (Bp.E.R.s.m.); while M. and P.p.m. have çvaçavarta , and W. çaçavarta . The occurrence of çavartá in TS. (v. 7. 23 1 : also in connection with ū́badhya ) determined the reading of our text. But our pada -text divides the word (Bp. çva॰vartá; D.Kp. ça॰v- ), which favors the reading çva- , since it implies a combination of the two recognizably independent words çvan and varta , 'occurring in dogs,' or something of the sort. Ppp. apparently has çivaratrebhyo . ⌊Roth suggests that çavarta may be for çavavarta 'Aaswurm, Made.'⌋

commentaries.whitney: With his horns he pushes the demon; with his eye he slays ruin; with his ears he hears what is excellent—he who is the inviolable lord of kine.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in a, b rakṣa riṣad rātī . The Prāt. (ii. 70) notes that the reading in d is not yás pát- . Some of the mss. (Bp.I.K.) accent aghnyàs .

commentaries.whitney: With a hundred-fold sacrifice he sacrifices; the fires burn him not; all the gods quicken him, who makes offering of a bull to a Brahman.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The last pāda is the same with 9 d . Ppp. has sarve instead of viçve in c .

commentaries.whitney: Having given a bull to Brahmans, one makes his mind wider; he beholds ( ava-paç ) prosperity of the inviolable [kine] in his own stall.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in a brāhmaṇāya vṛṣabhaṁ , and in d vi paçyatu . In a , we have to combine (as not very rarely elsewhere) -bhya rṣ- .

commentaries.whitney: Let there be kine, let there be progeny, also let there be own strength; let the gods approve all that for the giver of a bull.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. puts tat after sarvam in c .

commentaries.whitney: Let this burly ( pípāna ) one, a very Indra, bestow conspicuous wealth; let this one [bestow] a well-milking cow, constantly with calf; let him yield ( duh ) inspired will beyond the sky.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. has very different readings, which in part are less unacceptable than those of our text: for a, b , ayaṁ pipānā indriyaṁ gayāṁ bibharti tejanī: in d , vipaçyataṁ puro divaḥ . ⌊For pípāna , cf. Bloomfield, AJP. xii. 443.⌋

commentaries.whitney: Of reddish form, clouded (? nabhasá ), vigor-giving, vehemence of Indra, all-formed, he hath come to us, assigning to us life-time and progeny; and with abundances of wealth let him attach himself to ( abhi-sac ) us.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The last half-verse agrees nearly with xviii. 4. 62 c, d , where dádhatas and sacadhvam make better meter. It is not impossible to resolve asmábhi-am in c , but sacantām , which some of the mss. read (P.p.m.W.D.), is forbidden by the sense. Ppp. has a wholly different line: prajām asmabhyaṁ dadhato rayiṁ ca dīrghāyutvāya çataçāradāya . ⌊Bloomfield translates the verse at ZDMG. xlviii. 566, but overlooks the accent of nabhasó: cf. támas-ā and tamasā́ ( saṁhitā -form at xi. 9. 22).⌋

commentaries.whitney: Here in this stall, O closeness ( upapárcana ), be thou close unto us; unto [us] what seed the bull has; unto [us], O Indra, thy heroism.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This is a variant of RV. vi. 28. 8 (with which TB. ii. 8. 8 12 and LÇS. iii. 3. 4 precisely agree); RV. has, for a, b , úpe ’dám upapárcanam āsú góṣū́ ’pa pṛcyatām , with rétasi for yád rétas in c , and vīryè at the end: a very different sense; the Pet. Lexx. understand upa-pṛc as signifying here sexual union. We have to combine irregularly goṣṭho ’pa in order to rectify the meter of b ; the Anukr. does not heed the irregularity.

items.samhita_patha: ए॒तं वो॒ युवा॑नं॒ प्रति॑ दध्मो॒ अत्र॒ तेन॒ क्रीड॑न्तीश्चरत॒ वशाँ॒ अनु॑। मा नो॑ हासिष्ट ज॒नुषा॑ सुभागा रा॒यश्च॒ पोषै॑र॒भि नः॑ सचध्वम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: This young male we set toward you here; with him go ye (fem.) playing according to your wills; abandon us not with birth, ye wellportioned ones; and with abundances of wealth attach yourselves to us.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The last pāda is the same with xviii. 4. 62 d . The verse is found, in much more acceptable form, in TS. (iii. 3. 9 1 , followed, after one intervening verse, by our vss. 5, 4 above) and PGS. (iii. 9. 6, disagreeing with TS. in only one word); they read, for a , etáṁ yúvānam pári (but PGS. patiṁ ) vo dadāmi (omitting atra ); in b , priyéṇa for váçāṅ ánu; in c , çāpta for hāsiṣṭa; and, for d , rāyás póṣeṇa sám iṣā́ madema (nearly our iii. 15. 8 c ). Ppp. agrees with our text, only combining dadhmo ‘tra in a . But for the accent of janúṣā (in TS. also), we might render, with Stenzler, 'ye who are by birth well-portioned.' Bp.R.p.m. have at end of c subhagās . The Anukr. weakly calls the verse (12 + 12: 11 + 11) a jagatī , in spite of the triṣṭubh cadence of its first pāda. It is quoted in Kāuç. 24. 21, to accompany the sending away of an older bull and the release of a new one. ⌊See also note to Kāuç. 25. 24.⌋ ⌊Here ends the second anuvāka with 2 hymns and 55 verses. The quoted Anukr. says " sāhasre "⌋

commentaries.whitney: Conduct him hither; take hold; let him go, foreknowing, unto the world of the well-doing; crossing the great darknesses variously, let the goat step unto the third firmament ( nā́ka ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. has, in c , vipaçyaṁ for mahānti: cf. our 3 c . The first six verses of the hymn are quoted in their order in Kāuç. 64. 6-16 (vs. 1 also in 64. 27) in connection with the bringing in, slaughtering, and cooking of a goat; vss. 1 and 2 also in Vāit. 10. 14, 15, in connection with the sacrifice of an animal. This verse is called by the Anukr. simply a triṣṭubh , although its first half is very irregular (8 + 13).

commentaries.whitney: I lead thee about as portion for Indra, as patron ( sūrí ) for the sacrificer at this sacrifice; whoever hate us, them take hold after; innocent ( ánāgas ) [are] the sacrificer's heroes.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The verse in Ppp. (as noted above) follows what corresponds to our vs. 24, and has, for a, b , ind. bh. çamitā kṛṇotvaṁ yajña yajñapatiç ca sūriḥ; and, for d , ariṣṭā vīrā yajamānāç ca sarve .

items.samhita_patha_plain: इन्द्राय भागं परि त्वा नयाम्यस्मिन्यज्ञे यजमानाय सूरिम्। ये नो द्विषन्त्यनु तान्रभस्वानागसो यजमानस्य वीराः ॥

items.samhita_patha: प्र प॒दोऽव॑ नेनिग्धि॒ दुश्च॑रितं॒ यच्च॒चार॑ शु॒द्धैः श॒फैरा क्र॑मतां प्रजा॒नन्। ती॒र्त्वा तमां॑सि बहु॒धा वि॒पश्य॑न्न॒जो नाक॒मा क्र॑मतां तृ॒तीय॑म् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Away from his foot wash thou down the evil walk that he walked ( car ); with cleansed hoofs let him step on, foreknowing; crossing the darknesses, variously looking abroad let the goat step unto the third firmament.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Or padás in a may be accus. pl.; the redundancy of the pāda, in sense and meter, is an indication of intrusion; but the mode of its reduction to proper shape is not obvious, and Ppp. gives no help. Ppp. has, instead of our c, d , te jyotiṣmantaṁ sukṛtāl lokam īpsan tṛtīye nāke adhi vikramasva .

items.samhita_patha_plain: प्र पदोऽव नेनिग्धि दुश्चरितं यच्चचार शुद्धैः शफैरा क्रमतां प्रजानन्। तीर्त्वा तमांसि बहुधा विपश्यन्नजो नाकमा क्रमतां तृतीयम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: अनु॑छ्य श्या॒मेन॒ त्वच॑मे॒तां वि॑शस्तर्यथाप॒र्व१॒॑सिना॒ माभि मं॑स्थाः। माभि द्रु॑हः परु॒शः क॑ल्पयैनं तृ॒तीये॒ नाके॒ अधि॒ वि श्र॑यैनम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Cut along this skin with the dark [metal], O slaughterer, joint by joint with the knife ( así ); do not plot against [him]; do not be hostile to [him]; prepare him joint-wise; set him up apart in the third firmament.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. has, for d , sukṛtām madhye adhi vi çraye ’mam . The Anukr. weakly calls the verse a jagatī , although it is a triṣṭubh with three redundant syllables (doubtless çyāména or viçastar ) in a . The pada -text divides paru॰çaḥ , by Prāt. iv. 19.

items.samhita_patha_plain: अनुछ्य श्यामेन त्वचमेतां विशस्तर्यथापर्व१सिना माभि मंस्थाः। माभि द्रुहः परुशः कल्पयैनं तृतीये नाके अधि वि श्रयैनम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: ऋ॒चा कु॒म्भीमध्य॒ग्नौ श्र॑या॒म्या सि॑ञ्चोद॒कमव॑ धेह्येनम्। प॒र्याध॑त्ता॒ग्निना॑ शमितारः शृ॒तो ग॑च्छतु सु॒कृतां॒ यत्र॑ लो॒कः ॥

commentaries.whitney: With a verse I set the kettle upon the fire; pour thou on the water; set him down; set [him] about with fire, ye quellers; when cooked, let him go where is the world of the well-doing.
commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊Partly prose—"vss." 16, 20-22, 31-36; also considerable parts of 23-30.⌋ Found for the most part also in Pāipp., but not all together, nor even all in the same book; the greater part of the vss. (1, 3-6, 8, 7, 11, 9, 12, 10, 13-15, 19-21, 23, 24, 2) occur in xvi.; vss. 16, 17, 37 (part) in iii.; vss. 27, 28 in viii.; vss. 24-26, 31-36 are represented by similar, but briefer and very corrupt material, in xvi.; vss. 18, 22, 37 (part), 38 are wanting ⌊apparently also 29-30⌋. Three of the verses are quoted in Vāit., and more in Kāuç.: see under the verses. Translated: Muir, v. 304-6 (parts); Ludwig, p. 435; Henry, 93, 133; Griffith, i. 442. Ppp. has instead, for a , bhūmyāṁ bhūmim adhi dhārayāmi; and, in b , abhi for ava . The successive parts of the verse are quoted in Kāuç. 64. 11-15, to accompany corresponding acts. The Anukr. does not heed the redundant syllable in d .

items.samhita_patha_plain: ऋचा कुम्भीमध्यग्नौ श्रयाम्या सिञ्चोदकमव धेह्येनम्। पर्याधत्ताग्निना शमितारः शृतो गच्छतु सुकृतां यत्र लोकः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Step up from here, if thou hast been completely heated, from the heated pot on to the third firmament; thou, a fire, hast come into being out of fire; conquer [thy way] unto that world of light.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation of a implies the emendation to átapthās , which seems very probable; nearly all the mss. read ataptās (only E. áta- , P.M. ataptas ), which the edition has altered to átaptas . Of the reading in Ppp. I have no note; Ppp. reads for d jyotiṣmo acha sukṛtāṁ yatra lokaḥ; our d is found (nearly) as its 8 d .

items.samhita_patha_plain: उत्क्रामातः परि चेदतप्तस्तप्ताच्चरोरधि नाकं तृतीयम्। अग्नेरग्निरधि सं बभूविथ ज्योतिष्मन्तमभि लोकं जयैतम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: The goat [is] Agni, and they call the goat light; they say that the goat is to be given by one living to a priest ( brahmán ); the goat, given in this world by one having faith, smites far away the darknesses.
commentaries.whitney_notes: For the first two words Ppp. reads ajam evā ’gnim; in b , it puts jīvatā after brahmaṇe . The redundant syllable in b is not noticed by the Anukr. ⌊See note under 8.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: अजो अग्निरजमु ज्योतिराहुरजं जीवता ब्रह्मणे देयमाहुः। अजस्तमांस्यप हन्ति दूरमस्मिंल्लोके श्रद्दधानेन दत्तः ॥

items.samhita_patha: पञ्चौ॑दनः पञ्च॒धा वि क्र॑मतामाक्रं॒स्यमा॑न॒स्त्रीणि॒ ज्योतीं॑षि। ई॑जा॒नानां॑ सु॒कृतां॒ प्रेहि॒ मध्यं॑ तृ॒तीये॒ नाके॒ अधि॒ वि श्र॑यस्व ॥

commentaries.whitney: Having five rice-dishes, let him step out five-fold, about to step unto the three lights; go thou forth to the midst of the well-doing that have made offerings; spread out ( vi-çri ) upon the third firmament.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The last pāda is the same with xviii. 4. 3 e ; Ppp. has instead jyotiṣmantam abhi lokaṁ jayā ’smāi , with which compare our 6 d . The Anukr. passes in silence the irregularities of the second pāda. ⌊Cf. Oldenberg, ZDMG. l. 449.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: पञ्चौदनः पञ्चधा वि क्रमतामाक्रंस्यमानस्त्रीणि ज्योतींषि। ईजानानां सुकृतां प्रेहि मध्यं तृतीये नाके अधि वि श्रयस्व ॥

commentaries.whitney: Ascend, O goat, to where is the world of the well-doing; like an expelled çarabhá mayest thou move ( eṣ ) across difficult places; given, with five rice-dishes, to a priest ( brahmán ), he shall rejoice the giver with rejoicing.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads kramasva instead of roha in a , and reads çalabhas 'locust,' which is more sensible, in b ; our d is its 10 d , with dhātāram instead of dā- . The Anukr. treats the second pāda as regular, and it can, indeed, be read by violence into 11 syllables.

items.samhita_patha_plain: अजा रोह सुकृतां यत्र लोकः शरभो न चत्तोऽति दुर्गाण्येषः। पञ्चौदनो ब्रह्मणे दीयमानः स दातारं तृप्त्या तर्पयाति ॥

commentaries.whitney: The goat sets him that has given it on the three-firmamented, three-heavened, three-backed back of the firmament; being given with five rice-dishes to a priest, thou art a single milch-cow, all-formed, wish-yielding.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in b sukṛtāṁ lake for nākasya pṛṣṭhe; and our d is its 9 d , with the intrusive dhenus left out. The verse, in spite of its irregularity, is by the Anukr. reckoned simply a jagatī (11 + 12: 11 + 12 [13?]).

items.samhita_patha_plain: अजस्त्रिनाके त्रिदिवे त्रिपृष्ठे नाकस्य पृष्ठे ददिवांसं दधाति। पञ्चौदनो ब्रह्मणे दीयमानो विश्वरूपा धेनुः कामदुघास्येका ॥

commentaries.whitney: This third light of yours, O Fathers, the goat with five rice-dishes one gives to a priest; the goat, given in this world by one having faith, smites far away the darknesses.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The second half-verse is identical with 7 c, d above. Ppp. has, for d , pañcodano brahmaṇe dīyamānaḥ (our 9 c , 10 c ).

commentaries.whitney: Desiring to obtain the world of the well-doing that have made offerings, one gives to a priest a goat with five rice-dishes; do thou conquer complete attainment ( vyā̀pti ) unto that world; be he, accepted, propitious to us.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. begins pra jyotiṣmantaṁ sukṛtāṁ lok-; and reads c, d thus: sa vyāpo neṅṣ abhi lokaṁ jayā ’sme çivo ‘smabhyaṁ pratigṛhyate ‘dhi .

commentaries.whitney: The goat verily was born from the heat of the fire, wise, of the wise ( vípra ), of power, he the inspired one; what is offered, is bestowed, is conferred ( abhípūrta ), accompanied with váṣaṭ —that let the gods prepare in due season ( rtuçás ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The first pāda is identical with iv. 14. 1 a . Ludwig (also p. 370) proposes to emend in c to gūrtam abhigūrtam . Part of the mss. blunderingly accent ṛtuçàs in d . Ppp. has in b vayodha instead of vipaqcit, and in c puts purtam before istam. The last two padas are irregular, but the Anukr. takes no notice of it. ⌊Pāda c is a good jagatī; and d , a good triṣṭubh , if we read devā́sas , or (with Henry) tád íd .⌋

commentaries.whitney: A home-woven garment he may give, also gold as sacrificial gift; so he fully obtains the worlds that are heavenly and that are earthly.

items.samhita_patha: ए॒तास्त्वा॒जोप॑ यन्तु॒ धाराः॑ सो॒म्या दे॒वीर्घृ॒तपृ॑ष्ठा मधु॒श्चुतः॑। स्त॑भान पृ॑थि॒वीमु॒त द्यां नाक॑स्य पृ॒ष्ठेऽधि॑ स॒प्तर॑श्मौ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Unto thee, O goat, let these streams of soma ( somyá ) go, divine, ghee-backed, honey-dripping; establish thou earth and sky, upon the seven-rayed back of the firmament.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The mss. in general (not P.M.) accent ája in a . They are rather evenly divided between ádhi and ‘dhi in d (W.I.O.R.T.K. have ‘dhi ). Compare with a, b the refrain to iv. 34. 5-7. Ppp. reads for a : etās tvā dadhārā ’cchamayanti viçvatās somyaṁ; ⌊ somyaṁ would seem to be the beginning of Ppp's b ;⌋ in c, d , for uta...pṛṣṭhe , it gives divaṁ sadasva nāke tiṣṭhāsy . Pādas b, c are metrically irregular, but the Anukr. does not heed it.

commentaries.whitney: A goat art thou; O goat, heaven-going ( svar-gá ) art thou; by thee the An̄girases foreknew [their] world; that pure ( púṇya ) world would I fain foreknow.
commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊Prose.⌋ The translation of a is according to the accent of the vocative ája; there may be a play on words between ajá 'goat' and ajá 'unborn': 'unborn art thou, O goat' (emending to aja ). Ppp. reads for c taṁ lokaṁ anu pra jñeṣma . ⌊This vs. and the next are in its iii.⌋ The definition of the meter by the Anukr. seems senseless (7 [8?] + 11: 8 = 26). The third pāda is VS. xx. 25 c .

commentaries.whitney: Both truth and right its eyes, all truth [and] faith its breath, the virā́j its head; this verily is an unlimited offering, namely ( yát ) the goat with five rice-dishes.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The second satyam in vs. 21 is doubtless a corrupt reading, and the Ppp. version indicates that we should have instead rūpám ('the universe its form,' instead of 'all truth'). Ppp. reads, for the two verses: ajaṣ pañcāudano vy akramaia tasyo ’ra iyam abhavad udaram antarikṣam: dyāuṣ ṭe pṛṣṭhaṁ diçaṣ pārçve: dīçaç cā ’tidīçaç ca çṛn̄ge satyaṁ ca ṛtaṁ ca cakṣuṣī viçvarūpaṁ çraddhā etc. All the saṁhitā -mss. read ca rtáṁ (instead of ca ṛtáṁ ) near the beginning of vs. 21. The text of the Anukr. is apparently defective, leaving out the metrical definition of vss. 20-22 and vs. 25.

commentaries.whitney_notes: Wanting in Ppp., as noted above.

commentaries.whitney: He should not split its bones; he should not suck out its marrow; taking it all together, he should cause it to enter here and here.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Or, 'should cause this and this to enter'; the sense is obscure. Ppp. reads in c sarvāṇi for sarvam enam . By calling the verse a purauṣṇih , the Anukr. intends that its first two pādas be read as one, of 12 syllables. The Kāuç. quotes (66. 31, 32; next after quotations of verses from hymn 3) both halves of the verse, the latter to accompany the act of piercing an object and scattering it into a pit filled with water.

commentaries.whitney: This and this verily becomes its form; therewith one makes it come together; food, greatness, refreshment it yields ( duh ) to him who gives a goat with five rice-dishes, with the light of sacrificial gifts.

commentaries.whitney: Five gold ornaments ( rukmá ), five new garments, five milch-cows milking his desire come to be his who gives a goat with etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This verse, of which at least the first pāda is metrical (11 + 13: 15 = 39) is left undescribed in the Anukr. It (or vs. 26, both having the same pratīka ) is quoted in Kāuç. 64. 25. ⌊More nearly, 'Five milch-cows become wish-milking for him who,' that is, 'yield or grant to him his wishes who' etc.⌋

commentaries.whitney: Five gold ornaments become light for him; his garments become a defense for his body, he attains the heavenly ( svargá ) world, who gives a goat with etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Here are plainly four pādas, of which the first three are metrical, with the refrain added (11 + 11: 8 + 15); the definition of the Anukr. seems to imply 11 + 10: 8 + 7 + 9 = 45 syllables, or a bhurik triṣṭubh .

commentaries.whitney: Whoever (fem.) having gained a former husband, then gains another later one—if ( ca ) they (dual) shall give a goat with five rice-dishes, they shall not be separated.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The mss., as usual in such cases, read vitvā́ in a ; and all but Bp. strangely accent anyàm in b . Ppp. reads pacatas for dadātas in d . ⌊This vs. and the next are in Ppp's viii.⌋

commentaries.whitney_notes: The Anukr. treats the prose refrain of vss. 22, 24-26 as a half anuṣṭubh in the second line of this verse. Ppp. reads instead ajaṁ ca pañcāudanaṁ dadat .

commentaries.whitney_notes: The Anukr. takes no notice of the redundant syllable in b . ⌊Perhaps it balances the redundancy of b with the deficiency of c .⌋

commentaries.whitney_notes: Nor does the Anukr. heed the deficient syllables in b of this verse. ⌊We might render jánitrīm mātáram by 'the mother that bore [me].'⌋

commentaries.whitney: Whoever knows the season "torrid" ( nāídāgha ) by name—that verily is the season "torrid" by name, namely ( yát ) the goat with five rice-dishes; he indeed burns out the fortune of his unfriendly foe ( bhrā́tṛvya ), he thrives ( bhū ) by himself, who gives a goat with five rice-dishes, with the light of sacrificial gifts.

commentaries.whitney: Whoever knows the season "up-going" by name, each up-going fortune of his unfriendly foe he takes to himself; that verily is the season "up-going" by name, namely the goat etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: These four verses agree in number of syllables, and the name given them by the Anukr. ( prakṛti ) demands 84; this number it is possible to make out by resolutions of saṁdhi , though the natural reading gives only 80 (10 + 20: 15: 20 + 15 = 80). Saṁyatī́m॰saṁyatīn in vs. 33 b is quoted by the commentary under Prāt. iv. 44, as an example of a repeated separable word which gives up in pada -text its individual separation in favor of that between the repetitions. Read in 32 c yád ajáḥ (an accent-sign gone), and supply an omitted mark of punctuation after datte in 33.

commentaries.whitney: Whoever knows the season "overcoming" ( abhibhū́ ) by name, each overcoming fortune of his unfriendly foe he takes to himself; that verily is the season "overcoming" by name, namely the goat etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This verse has six more syllables than the preceding ones, and the Anukr. gives it a name ( ākṛti ) applying properly to 88 syllables. In c read eṣá for eṣā́ .

commentaries.whitney: Cook ye the goat and the five rice-dishes; let all the quarters, like-minded, united ( sadhryàñc ), with the intermediate directions, accept that of thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: All the mss. (except D.) read at the end tá ( pada -text té ) before etám; our edition emends to ta; the word could better be spared altogether. Ppp. has (in iii.) only the first pāda. The Anukr. describes the verse as if this pāda as well as the other two were metrical.

commentaries.whitney: Let them defend this of thine for thee; to them I offer ( hu ) sacrificial butter, this oblation.
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Them' is fem., designating the 'quarters' of vs. 37. The translation omits a te; it may be regarded as an ethical dative, anticipating the distincter túbhyam 'for thee' that follows. ⌊This hymn begins with ā́ naya; and, with its 38 vss., exceeds the norm by 18. The quoted Anukr. says aṣṭādaçā “”naya.” ⌋ ⌊The twentieth prapāṭhaka ends here. As in the cases of the tenth and eighteenth (ending at v. 7 and viii. 5), the prapāṭhaka -division here fails to coincide with the anuvāka -division.⌋

commentaries.whitney: Prajāpati and the most exalted one are his two horns, Indra his head, Agni his forehead, Yama his neck-joint.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The copula and the possessive, wherever read, are supplied in the translation. Ppp. omits yamaḥ kṛkāṭam . The verse has only 26 syllables (instead of 27).

items.samhita_patha: सोमो॒ राजा॑ म॒स्तिष्को॒ द्यौरु॑त्तरह॒नुः पृ॑थि॒व्य᳡धरह॒नुः ॥

commentaries.whitney: King Soma his brain, the sky his upper jaw, the earth his lower jaw.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. inserts, after mastiṣkas, satyaṁ cakṣur ṛtaṁ çrotre prāṇāpānāu nāmivate , and reads adharā for -rahanuḥ , adding after it agnir āsyaṁ . We are required to resolve pṛthivī adh- .

items.samhita_patha_plain: सोमो राजा मस्तिष्को द्यौरुत्तरहनुः पृथिव्य᳡धरहनुः ॥

items.samhita_patha: वि॒द्युज्जि॒ह्वा म॒रुतो॒ दन्ता॑ रे॒वती॑र्ग्री॒वाः कृत्ति॑का स्क॒न्धा घ॒र्मो वहः॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Lightning his tongue, the Maruts his teeth, the Revatīs his neck, the Kṛittikās his shoulders ( skandhā́s ), the hot drink ( gharmá ) his withers ( váha ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Váha is properly the "carrying" part, that on which the yoke rests. The Revatīs and Kṛttikās, two asterisms, in Pisces and Taurus respectively; their connection with the parts to which they are assigned is, as in nearly all the other cases in this hymn, of the most purely imaginary and meaningless kind. Ppp. has only as far as dantāṣ , following it with pavamānaṣ prāṇaḥ . Read in our text grīvā́ḥ ( visarga -sign omitted). The pada -text has kṛ́ttikāḥ , and some of the mss., as usual, retain the ḥ before the following sk . The verse has but 23 syllables (unless we analyze jihu-ā́ ).

items.samhita_patha_plain: विद्युज्जिह्वा मरुतो दन्ता रेवतीर्ग्रीवाः कृत्तिका स्कन्धा घर्मो वहः ॥

items.samhita_patha: विश्वं॑ वा॒युः स्व॒र्गो लो॒कः कृ॑ष्ण॒द्रं वि॒धर॑णी निवे॒ष्यः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Vāyu his all ( víçvam ), the heavenly world his kṛṣṇadrá , the whirlwind (? niveṣyà ) his separator (? vidháraṇī ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The words here in part (and in the last clause the distinction of subject and predicate) are wholly obscure. The pada -text divides kṛṣṇa॰drám ('black-runner'?). Many of the mss. (E.O.D.R.T.K.) accent niveṣyáḥ . Ppp. reads viçvaṁ vāyuṣ kaṇṭhas svargo lokaṣ kṛṣṇadra vyadriṇī vivaçvaḥ; and then it adds the omitted part of our vs. 3 except vahaḥ at the end.

commentaries.whitney: The falcon his breast ( kroḍá ), the atmosphere his belly (? pājasyà ), Brihaspati his hump, the bṛhatī́s his vertebrae.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The sense of bṛhatī here is doubtful. Ppp. reads pājasyaṁ and inserts our vs. 7 after it ⌊continuing with bṛhasp -⌋. The required number of 24 syllables is made out by reading kroḍó ant- and pājasí-am .

items.samhita_patha: मि॒त्रश्च॒ वरु॑ण॒श्चांसौ॒ त्वष्टा॑ चार्य॒मा च॑ दो॒षणी॑ महादे॒वो बा॒हू ॥

commentaries.whitney: Both Mitra and Varuṇa his (two) shoulders ( áṅsa ), both Tvashṭar and Aryaman his (two) shanks ( doṣán ), the great god his fore-legs.
commentaries.whitney_notes: [ Brahman.—ekaḥ [ paryāyaḥ ]. ṣaḍviṅçaḥ. gavyaḥ. ] ⌊Prose.⌋ Found for the most part (for details, see under the verses) in Pāipp. xvi. also. Not noticed in Vāit., but quoted (vs. 1) in Kāuç. 66. 19, next after hymn 4 of this book. ⌊For the paryāya -hymns in general, see pages 471-2.⌋ Translated: Henry, 103, 139; Griffith, i. 453. By Ppp. the verse is inserted in our vs. 5, as there noted. The verse has 23 syllables, but is not 'ant-waisted,' as it divides 8 + 9 + 6.

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines gandharvā ’ps- . The so-called purauṣṇih divides 10 + 12 + 5 = 27 syllables.

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads manuṣyā ”ntrāṇy ātrā ud- , putting the verse after our 12. In order to make out 18 syllables, we have to resolve -ṣí-a āntrā́ṇi at- .

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. inverts the order of the two clauses, and reads ūvadhyam .

commentaries.whitney_notes: In Ppp. this verse follows our 15, and there is added bhūtyāṣ prajāyāṣ paçūnāṁ bhavati ya evaṁ veda .

commentaries.whitney_notes: This verse is wanting in Ppp. The metrical definition requires restoration of the a of açvínā .

commentaries.whitney: Indra when standing eastward, Yama when standing southward;

commentaries.whitney: Dhātar when standing westward, Savitar when standing northward;
commentaries.whitney_notes: The metrical definition requires the resolution dhātā́ údan̄ . Read savitā́ (an accent-sign slipped out of place).

commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -mss. have the false accent pra॰ā́ptaḥ (for prá॰āptaḥ ). ⌊Ppp. reads tṛṇān prāptas soma rājā .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: तृणानि प्राप्तः सोमो राजा ॥

commentaries.whitney: Mitra when looking, delight ( ānandá ) when turned this way;
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. unites this verse with the preceding, and inverts the order of the two clauses of this verse, reading rājā ”nṛtā ”nandaḥ īkṣamāṇo mitrāvaruṇo .

commentaries.whitney_notes: As to visalpakam , instead of the visalyakam of the edition, see under vi. 127. 1. For the obscure kan̄kūṣa Ppp. has kaṅkukha , and for b it reads çuktivalçaṁ vilohitam .

commentaries.whitney: Whatever one makes a man dumb (? pramóta ), makes [him] blind—every head-disease etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Dumb' for pramóta is Zimmer's conjecture; the word is wholly obscure, and form, accent, and meter make it suspicious; one is tempted to conjecture prámohitam; but muh with prefix pra is not a Vedic combination. The Anukr. takes no notice of the defective pāda.

items.samhita_patha: यस्य॑ भी॒मः प्र॑तीका॒श उ॑द्वे॒पय॑ति॒ पूरु॑षम्। त॒क्मानं॑ वि॒श्वशा॑रदं ब॒हिर्निर्म॑न्त्रयामहे ॥
items.pada_patha: यस्य॑ । भी॒म: । प्र॒ति॒ऽका॒श: । उ॒त्ऽवे॒पय॑ति । पुरु॑षम् । त॒क्मान॑म् । वि॒श्वऽशा॑रदम् । ब॒हि: । नि: । म॒न्त्र॒या॒म॒हे॒ ॥१३.६॥

commentaries.whitney: Of whom the fearful aspect makes a man tremble—the takmán of every autumn we expel out [of thee] by incantation.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads pāuruṣam in b , and, for c, d , takmānaṁ çītaṁ rūraṁ ca taṁ tve nir man- : cf. v. 22. 10, 13.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यस्य भीमः प्रतीकाश उद्वेपयति पूरुषम्। तक्मानं विश्वशारदं बहिर्निर्मन्त्रयामहे ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: यस्य । भीम: । प्रतिऽकाश: । उत्ऽवेपयति । पुरुषम् । तक्मानम् । विश्वऽशारदम् । बहि: । नि: । मन्त्रयामहे ॥१३.६॥

items.samhita_patha: य ऊ॒रू अ॑नु॒सर्प॒त्यथो॒ एति॑ ग॒वीनि॑के। यक्ष्मं॑ ते अ॒न्तरङ्गे॑भ्यो ब॒हिर्निर्म॑न्त्रयामहे ॥

commentaries.whitney: The yákṣma that creeps along the thighs, that goes also to the groins, from thy limbs within we expel etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in c balāsam for yakṣmaṁ te [cf. our 8 c and under 9⌋.

items.samhita_patha_plain: य ऊरू अनुसर्पत्यथो एति गवीनिके। यक्ष्मं ते अन्तरङ्गेभ्यो बहिर्निर्मन्त्रयामहे ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: य: । ऊरू इति । अनुऽसर्पति । अथो इति । एति । गवीनिके इति । यक्ष्मम् । ते । अन्त: । अङ्गेभ्य: । बहि: । नि: । मन्त्रयामहे ॥१३.७॥

items.samhita_patha: यदि॒ कामा॑दपका॒माद्धृद॑या॒ज्जाय॑ते॒ परि॑। हृ॒दो ब॒लास॒मङ्गे॑भ्यो ब॒हिर्निर्म॑न्त्रयामहे ॥

commentaries.whitney: If it is born out of desire, of aversion, of the heart—the balā́sa from thy heart, thy limbs we expel etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Found also (except vs. 4) in Pāipp. xvi. Not noticed in Vāit., but quoted (vs. 1) in Kāuç. 32. 18, in a remedial ceremony. ⌊The last two verses are specified (32. 19) as used "with worship of the sun."⌋ Translated: Zimmer, p. 378; Henry, 105, 141; Griffith, i. 455; Bloomfield, 45, 600.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यदि कामादपकामाद्धृदयाज्जायते परि। हृदो बलासमङ्गेभ्यो बहिर्निर्मन्त्रयामहे ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: यदि । कामात् । अपऽकामात् । हृदयात् । जायते । परि । हृद: । बलासम् । अङ्गेभ्य: । बहि:। नि: । मन्त्रयामहे ॥१३.८॥

items.samhita_patha: ह॑रि॒माणं॑ ते॒ अङ्गे॑भ्यो॒ऽप्वाम॑न्त॒रोदरा॑त्। य॑क्ष्मो॒धाम॒न्तरा॒त्मनो॑ ब॒हिर्निर्म॑न्त्रयामहे ॥
items.pada_patha: ह॒रि॒माण॑म् । ते॒ । अङ्गे॑भ्य: । अ॒प्वाम् । अ॒न्त॒रा । उ॒दरा॑त् । य॒क्ष्म॒:ऽधाम् । अ॒न्त: । आ॒त्मन॑: । ब॒हि: । नि: । म॒न्त्र॒या॒म॒हे॒ ॥१३.९॥

commentaries.whitney: Yellowness from thy limbs, apvā́ from thy belly within, the yákṣma -maker from thy self within we expel etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -text reads in c yakṣmaḥ॰dhā́m . The Prāt. takes no notice of the irregular form of the first member of the compound, as it does, superfluously (ii. 56), of the contrary treatment of çepas in çepa॰harṣaṇīm . In Ppp. our third pāda becomes the second, and for third we have nearly our 7 c : yakṣmaṁ te sarvam an̄gebhyo .

items.samhita_patha_plain: हरिमाणं ते अङ्गेभ्योऽप्वामन्तरोदरात्। यक्ष्मोधामन्तरात्मनो बहिर्निर्मन्त्रयामहे ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: हरिमाणम् । ते । अङ्गेभ्य: । अप्वाम् । अन्तरा । उदरात् । यक्ष्म:ऽधाम् । अन्त: । आत्मन: । बहि: । नि: । मन्त्रयामहे ॥१३.९॥

items.samhita_patha: आसो॑ ब॒लासो॒ भव॑तु॒ मूत्रं॑ भवत्वा॒मय॑त्। यक्ष्मा॑णां॒ सर्वे॑षां वि॒षं निर॑वोचम॒हं त्वत् ॥
items.pada_patha: आस॑: । ब॒लास॑: । भव॑तु । मूत्र॑म् । भ॒व॒तु॒ । आ॒मय॑त् । यक्ष्मा॑णाम् । सर्वे॑षाम् । वि॒षम् । नि: । अ॒वो॒च॒म् । अ॒हम् । त्वत् ॥१३.१०॥

commentaries.whitney: Let the balā́sa become ash, let it become sickening urine; the poison of all yákṣmas have I exorcised from thee.

items.samhita_patha_plain: आसो बलासो भवतु मूत्रं भवत्वामयत्। यक्ष्माणां सर्वेषां विषं निरवोचमहं त्वत् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: आस: । बलास: । भवतु । मूत्रम् । भवतु । आमयत् । यक्ष्माणाम् । सर्वेषाम् । विषम् । नि: । अवोचम् । अहम् । त्वत् ॥१३.१०॥

items.samhita_patha: ब॒हिर्बिलं॒ निर्द्र॑वतु॒ काहा॑बाहं॒ तवो॒दरा॑त्। यक्ष्मा॑णां॒ सर्वे॑षां वि॒षं निर॑वोचम॒हं त्वत् ॥
items.pada_patha: ब॒हि: । ब‍िल॑म् । नि: । द्र॒व॒तु॒ । काहा॑बाहम् । तव॑ । उ॒दरा॑त् । यक्ष्मा॑णाम् । सर्वे॑षाम् । वि॒षम् । नि: । अ॒वो॒च॒म् । अ॒हम् । त्वत् ॥१३.११॥

commentaries.whitney: Forth at the orifice let it run out, the kā́hābāha , from thy belly; the poison of all etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊Literally 'to the orifice'; Henry "vers le trou," i.e. "par l'anus."⌋ The Pet. Lexx. plausibly conjecture kāhābāha to be an imitative term for rumbling in the bowels; it may also possibly be understood as used adverbially, like bāl in i. 3. Ppp. has a quite different reading for b : kahāvalaṁ tvaṅdarā .

items.samhita_patha_plain: बहिर्बिलं निर्द्रवतु काहाबाहं तवोदरात्। यक्ष्माणां सर्वेषां विषं निरवोचमहं त्वत् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: बहि: । ब‍िलम् । नि: । द्रवतु । काहाबाहम् । तव । उदरात् । यक्ष्माणाम् । सर्वेषाम् । विषम् । नि: । अवोचम् । अहम् । त्वत् ॥१३.११॥

items.samhita_patha: उ॒दरा॑त्ते क्लो॒म्नो नाभ्या॒ हृद॑या॒दधि॑। यक्ष्मा॑णां॒ सर्वे॑षां वि॒षं निर॑वोचम॒हं त्वत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Out of thy belly, lung, navel, heart, the poison of all etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. rectifies the meter of a by inserting pari before klomnas , and makes c, d agree with our 9 c, d . The Anukr. brings out an uṣṇih (28 syll.) by unnaturally refusing to make the resolutions nābhi-ās and tu-at ⌊and scanning as 6 + 7: 8 + 7⌋.

items.samhita_patha_plain: उदरात्ते क्लोम्नो नाभ्या हृदयादधि। यक्ष्माणां सर्वेषां विषं निरवोचमहं त्वत् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: उदरात् । ते । क्लोम्न: । नाभ्या: । हृदयात् । अधि । यक्ष्माणम् । सर्वेषाम् । विषम् । नि: । अवोचम् । अहम् । त्वत् ॥१३.१२॥

items.samhita_patha: याः सी॒मानं॑ विरु॒जन्ति॑ मू॒र्धानं॒ प्रत्य॑र्ष॒णीः। अहिं॑सन्तीरनाम॒या निर्द्र॑वन्तु ब॒हिर्बिल॑म् ॥

commentaries.whitney: They that break apart the crown, rushers against the head ( mūrdhán )—not injuring, free from disease, let them run out, out at the orifice.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The 'they' in this and the following verses (13-18) is fem. The Pet. Lexx. take arṣaṇī́ in b as an independent noun (it is found only here), and conjecture it to mean 'pricking pains.'

items.samhita_patha_plain: याः सीमानं विरुजन्ति मूर्धानं प्रत्यर्षणीः। अहिंसन्तीरनामया निर्द्रवन्तु बहिर्बिलम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: या: । सीमानम् । विऽरुजन्ति । मूर्धानम् । प्रति । अर्षणी: । अहिंसन्ती: । अनामया: । नि: । द्रवन्तु । बहि: । बिलम् ॥१३.१३॥

items.samhita_patha: या हृद॑यमुप॒र्षन्त्य॑नुत॒न्वन्ति॒ कीक॑साः। अहिं॑सन्तीरनाम॒या निर्द्र॑वन्तु ब॒हिर्बिल॑म् ॥

commentaries.whitney: They that rush unto the heart, that stretch along the vertebrae—not injuring etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Prāt. iii. 47 prescribes the form uparṣánti (instead of upārṣánti: p. upa॰ṛṣánti ) in this and the two following verses. Ppp. reads every time upadiçanti .

items.samhita_patha_plain: या हृदयमुपर्षन्त्यनुतन्वन्ति कीकसाः। अहिंसन्तीरनामया निर्द्रवन्तु बहिर्बिलम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: या: । हृदयम् । उपऽऋषन्ति । अनुऽतन्वन्ति । कीकसा: । अहिंसन्ती: । अनामया: । नि: । द्रवन्तु । बहि: । बिलम् ॥१३.१४॥

items.samhita_patha: याः पा॒र्श्वे उ॑प॒र्षन्त्य॑नु॒निक्ष॑न्ति पृ॒ष्टीः। अहिं॑सन्तीरनाम॒या निर्द्र॑वन्तु ब॒हिर्बिल॑म् ॥

commentaries.whitney: They that rush unto the two sides, that stab ( nikṣ ) along the ribs—not injuring etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The Anukr. intends pārçvé to be read unresolved.

items.samhita_patha_plain: याः पार्श्वे उपर्षन्त्यनुनिक्षन्ति पृष्टीः। अहिंसन्तीरनामया निर्द्रवन्तु बहिर्बिलम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: या: । पार्श्वे इति । उपऽऋषन्ति । अनुऽनिक्षन्ति । पृष्टी: । अहिंसन्ती: । अनामया: । नि: । द्रवन्तु । बहि: । बिलम् ॥१३.१५॥

items.samhita_patha: यास्ति॒रश्चीः॑ उप॒र्षन्त्य॑र्ष॒णीर्व॒क्षणा॑सु ते। अहिं॑सन्तीरनाम॒या निर्द्र॑वन्तु ब॒हिर्बिल॑म् ॥

commentaries.whitney: They that rush on crosswise, rushers in thy belly ( vakṣáṇā )—not injuring etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in b vakṣaṇābhyaḥ , and omits the following te .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यास्तिरश्चीः उपर्षन्त्यर्षणीर्वक्षणासु ते। अहिंसन्तीरनामया निर्द्रवन्तु बहिर्बिलम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: या: । तिरश्ची: । उपऽऋषन्ति । अर्षणी: । वक्षणासु । ते । अहिंसन्ती: । अनामया: । नि: । द्रवन्तु । बहि: । बिलम् ॥१३.१६॥

items.samhita_patha: या गुदा॑ अनु॒सर्प॑न्त्या॒न्त्राणि॑ मो॒हय॑न्ति च। अहिं॑सन्तीरनाम॒या निर्द्र॑वन्तु ब॒हिर्बिल॑म् ॥

commentaries.whitney: They that creep along the intestines, and confound the entrails—not injuring etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in b yāpayanti for mohayanti . ⌊Roth most ingeniously suggests that the Ppp. reading may mean āntrā, ni-y-āmayanti . Or is yāpayanti to be taken in a sense quite like our English 'cause (the bowels) to move,' i.e. 'produce diarrhœa'?⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: या गुदा अनुसर्पन्त्यान्त्राणि मोहयन्ति च। अहिंसन्तीरनामया निर्द्रवन्तु बहिर्बिलम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: या: । गुदा: । अनुऽसर्पन्ति । आन्त्राणि । मोहयन्ति । च । अहिंसन्ती: । अनामया: । नि: । द्रवन्तु । बहि: । बिलम् ॥१३.१७॥

items.samhita_patha: या म॒ज्ज्ञो नि॒र्धय॑न्ति॒ परूं॑षि विरु॒जन्ति॑ च। अहिं॑सन्तीरनाम॒या निर्द्र॑वन्तु ब॒हिर्बिल॑म् ॥

commentaries.whitney: They that suck out the marrow, and break apart the joints—not injuring etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in a anusarpanti for nirdhayanti . We are to resolve maj-jñ-o to fill out the measure.

items.samhita_patha_plain: या मज्ज्ञो निर्धयन्ति परूंषि विरुजन्ति च। अहिंसन्तीरनामया निर्द्रवन्तु बहिर्बिलम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: या: । मज्ज्ञ: । नि:ऽधयन्ति । परूंषि । विऽरुजन्ति । च । अहिंसन्ती: । अनामया: । नि: । द्रवन्तु । बहि: । बिलम् ॥१३.१८॥

items.samhita_patha: ये अङ्गा॑नि म॒दय॑न्ति॒ यक्ष्मा॑सो रोप॒णास्तव॑। यक्ष्मा॑णां॒ सर्वे॑षां वि॒षं निर॑वोचम॒हं त्वत् ॥
items.pada_patha: ये । अङ्गा॑नि । म॒दय॑न्ति । यक्ष्मा॑स: । रो॒प॒णा: । तव॑ । यक्ष्मा॑णाम् । सर्वे॑षाम् । वि॒षम् । नि: । अ॒वो॒च॒म् । अ॒हम् । त्वत् ॥१३.१९॥

commentaries.whitney: They that intoxicate ( maday- ) the limbs, the yákṣmas , thy gripers—the poison of all yákṣmas have I exorcised from thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in b ropaṇā saha . Some of our mss. (P.M.O.p.m.) read yé ’n̄gāni .

items.samhita_patha_plain: ये अङ्गानि मदयन्ति यक्ष्मासो रोपणास्तव। यक्ष्माणां सर्वेषां विषं निरवोचमहं त्वत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Forth from thy feet, knees, hips, buttock, spine, nape the pangs, from thy head the disease have I made disappear.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads, after te, gulphābhyāṁ jan̄ghābhyāṁ jānubhyām ūrubhyāṁ çro. p. bh.; it reads ānūkyāt in c , and inserts before çīrṣṇas, grīvābhyas skandhebhyas . It is apparently the intrusion of arṣaṇī́s that spoils the meter in our c .

commentaries.whitney: Together the bones ( kapā́la ) of thy head, and the discusser ( vidhú ) of thy heart—arising, O Āditya, thou with thy rays hast made disappear the disease of the head, hast pacified the limb-splitter.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The first two pādas seem independent; an unfinished construction. The pada -text reads vi॰dhúḥ in b , as if it recognized in the word the root dhū + vi; this is not implausible, and the translation follows it (the simple "beat" of the Pet. Lexx. seems quite unacceptable; it might be 'palpitation'). But Ppp. reads instead vidus , and so do a part of our mss., namely, W.O.s.m.D.Kp. ⌊W. interlines a query over "discusser," which word he coins and uses in the sense 'shaker asunder.' "Discuss" in this sense is "obsolete except in surgical use."⌋ Ppp. further has, for our c etc.: udyat sūryādityo an̄gāni roma nakhāni sarvāṇi sadanāni nīnaçat . ⌊The fourth anuvāka , with 2 hymns and 48 verses, ends here. The quoted Anukr. says navadaçā ’pare ca .⌋

commentaries.whitney: Of this pleasant ( vāmá ) hoary invoker—of him the brother is the midmost stone (? áçna ); his third brother [is] ghee-backed; there I saw the lord of the people who hath seven sons.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The three brothers are explained as the three forms of Agni, in heaven, in the atmosphere (lightning), and on earth (sacrificial fire): the 'seven sons' are most probably his many flames. ⌊The collocation of madhyamó with bhrā́tā would seem more natural, considering the phrase tṛtī́yo bhrā́tā .

commentaries.whitney: Seven harness ( yuj ) a one-wheeled chariot; one horse, having seven names, draws ( vah ) [it]; of three naves [is] the wheel, unwasting, unassailed, whereon stand all these existences.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Doubtless the sun. The verse is repeated as xiii. 3. 18. It occurs also in TA. iii. 11. 8, with anarvāṁ yene ’mā v. bhuvanāni t. in c, d (the accent of the verse is too corrupt to heed).

commentaries.whitney_notes: RV. reads navante in c , and nā́ma in d .

commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Bears,' not in the sense of 'gives birth to,' but of 'carries' or 'supports' or the like.

commentaries.whitney: Let him who truly knows ⌊here⌋ tell ( brū ) the set-down track of this pleasant bird; the kine extract ( duh ) milk from his head; clothing themselves in a wrap, they have drunk water with the foot.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Explained as relating to the clouds and the sun. The verse is vs. 7 in RV., and also in Ppp.; the latter reads çīrṣṇā in c .

items.samhita_patha: अचि॑कित्वांश्चिकि॒तुष॑श्चि॒दत्र॑ क॒वीन्पृ॑च्छामि वि॒द्वनो॒ न वि॒द्वान्। वि यस्त॒स्तम्भ॒ षडि॒मा रजां॑स्य॒जस्य॑ रू॒पे किमपि॑ स्वि॒देक॑म् ॥

commentaries.whitney: I, not understanding ( cit ), ask here the understanding poets, I unknowing ( vid ), them that know; he who propped asunder these six spaces ( rájas ), in the form of the goat (? ajá )—was that also alone?
commentaries.whitney_notes: The sense of the last pāda is utterly obscure, and the version given only tentative; ajá is perhaps here really the 'unborn one,' as the translators render it. RV. reads in a ácikitvāñ cik- , and, in b , vidmáne , for which our vidvánas is apparently a mere corruption.

commentaries.whitney: The mother portioned the father in righteousness, for with meditation ( dhītí ), with mind, came together in the beginning she, repugnant, womb-sapped, pierced; paying homage, verily, they went unto encouragement.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The version is in part only mechanical. Ppp. combines ṛtā ”babh- in a , and reads jajñe at end of b .

commentaries.whitney: The mother was yoked to the pole of the sacrificial gift; the embryo stood among the wiles (? vṛjanī́ ); the calf bleated, looked after the cow of all forms, in the three distances ( yójana ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: [ Brahman.—dvāviṅçakam. vāmīyam ādityadevatyam adhyātmakaram. trāiṣṭubham: 12, 14, 16, 18. jagatī. ] This hymn and the following (except a few verses of the latter) are one Rig-Veda hymn, namely, i. 164, and but a small part of them occur in any other Vedic text. Both are found in Pāipp. xvi., in somewhat changed verse-order, as will be noted under the different verses below. Vāit. takes no notice of this hymn; in Kāuç. it (vs. 1) is quoted in 18. 25, with various others, in a ceremony for prosperity; and the gaṇamālā (see note to Kāuç. 18. 25) reckons it as belonging to the salila gaṇa . Translated: as RV. hymn, by Ludwig, no. 951; and Grassmann, ii. p. 456-460; also by M. Haug, under the tide, Vedische Räthselfragen und Räthselsprüche, Sb. der philos.-philol. Classe der k. bairischen Ak. der Wiss. , Bd. II., Heft 3, für 1875, München, 1876 (the essay, says Whitney, "casts extremely little light upon its labored obscurities"); further, with an elaborate comment touching the significance of its philosophic content, by Deussen, Geschichte , i. 1. 105-119; parts also by Muir, v. (see Index, p. 484), and Hillebrandt, Ved. Mythol. , i. (see Index, p. 542); and under the title, Zwei Sprüche über Leib und Seele , ZDMG. xlvi. 759 f., Roth explains two verses answering to our ix. 10. 8 and 16. Under the title. Das Räthsel vom Jahre , ZDMG. xlviii. 353, E. Windisch discusses the RV. verse answering to our vs. 12. Translated, moreover, as AV. hymn, by Henry, 107, 143; Griffith, i. 458. The critical remarks of Oldenberg, IFA. vi. 180-183, may also be consulted.—Further, von Schroeder, Der Rigveda bei den Kaṭhas , WZKM. xii. 282, reports variants for certain vss. of the RV. hymn which correspond to our vss. ix. 9. 9, 12, 17, 22 and ix. 10. 16.—Finally, A. Wünsche's essay. Das Rätsel vom Jahr und seinen Zeitabschnitten in der Weltlitteratur , may be cited in this connection; it is found in Zeitschrift für vergl. Litteraturgeschichte , N.F., ix. 425-456. ⌊Kaṭha variants, WZKM. xii. 282, vṛjanéṣv antáḥ and yojáneṣu .—Cf. IFA. vi. 180, as noted above.⌋

commentaries.whitney: The one, bearing three mothers [and] three fathers, stood upright; verily they do not exhaust him; on the back of yon sky the all-knowing ones talk a speech not found by all.
commentaries.whitney_notes: RV. reads glāpayanti at end of b ⌊and the translation follows that reading⌋, and, for d , viçvavídaṁ vā́cam áviçvaminvām . The pada -text reads glapayanta; Prāt. iv. 93 notes the case. Ppp. agrees with RV. in glāpayanti and viçvavidam .

commentaries.whitney: On the five-spoked circumvolving wheel on which stood all existences—its axle, much-burdened, is not heated; even from of old it is not severed with the nave.
commentaries.whitney_notes: RV. and Ppp. count this verse as 13, our version inverting the order of 11-13. In b , RV. reads tásminn ā́ tasthur bh. v. , and Ppp. samārohanti bh. v.; and RV. has çīryate for chidyate in d .

commentaries.whitney: The five-footed father, of twelve shapes ( -ā́kṛti ), they call rich in ground ( purīṣín ) in the far ( pára ) half of the sky; then these others call [him] set ( árpita ) in the lower outlook that is seven-wheeled, six-spoked.
commentaries.whitney_notes: RV. and Ppp. have the easier and better reading vicakṣaṇám in c , and Ppp. reads before it upari . ⌊The Kaṭha reading also is úpari , WZKM. xii. 282.⌋ Read in b páre (an accent sign slipped out of place). ⌊See Roth, KZ. xxvi. 66, and Windisch as cited in the introduction; cf. also IFA. vi. 181, as noted above.⌋

commentaries.whitney: The twelve-spoked wheel—for that is not to be worn out—revolves greatly about the sky of righteousness; there, O Agni, stood the sons, paired, seven hundred and twenty.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Here the 'twelve' and the 'seven hundred and twenty' are plainly the months, and the days and nights, of the year of 360 days. The verse, as noted above, is vs. 11 in RV. and Ppp. The more proper reading in b would be várvartti .
